radius 1 and the other two vertices on the circumference occurs when the two vertices are
positioned opposite each other, forming a diameter of the circle. In this configuration,
the triangle becomes an isosceles triangle with its base along the diameter and height
equal to the radius of the circle. The area can be calculated using the formula for the
area of a triangle, A = 1/2 * base * height. Here, the base is 2 (the diameter) and the
height is 1 (the radius), resulting in an area of A = 1/2 * 2 * 1 = 1. Thus, the maximum
area of the triangle is 1 square unit, achieved under these specific conditions.
